why: RESTORES A CODE THIS PRODUCT ALREADY HELD, and the second wrong clear the audit has written. #229 and #8474 both stood on TP - 050004 in the baseline. Two rows were then written about that page and they contradict each other: #8474's row says they are 'the same painting ... #229 is the framed piece shown whole; #8474 is a zoomed crop of it', while this row said 'This is a different photograph' and cleared #229 to nothing. #8474's row is the correct one. #229's featured image IS a room mockup, but that is not a reason it cannot be compared - enlarged 8x the framed print on the wall carries the whole composition of TP 04, and it agrees with the page on five independent points: the ornate pointed crest above the gold prabhavali arch, the twin garlands angling down and outward from the shoulders in red/white/green, the closed OVAL vanamala loop hanging to below the waist (an unusual shape, same position and proportion in both), the banded gold pillars flanking left and right, and lamp flames in the same two upper corners. WHY THE EARLIER PASS GOT IT WRONG: a room mockup prints the artwork small and under ambient light, so it renders darker and flatter than the book page does. That row judged on tone - 'a darker idol in a golden arch' - rather than on composition, and tone is exactly what a mockup changes. Composition is what survives it. NOTE ON THE CODE FORM: this row must carry the full six-digit code. TP is one of the two sections whose old and new numbering differ (absent => array(4)), so the short legacy form shifts - 'TP 05' resolves to TP - 050004 and 'TP 13' resolves to TP - 050012, while 'TP 04' resolves to nothing at all because old TP 04 never named a page. Sharing is correct rather than a clash: two listings of one picture, and the SKU letter keeps their SKUs apart
